Exploitation without full relief is Zang et al.'s prestress, which switches stability while some transitions stay unachievable. In [TERM-060](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-060.md)'s sense only the first touches frustration; the others act on its load and its consequences. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v9 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions are needed for it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)) and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Active |
| [CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) v4 | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." In [TERM-105](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-105.md)'s terms a savings buffer is a replenishable reserve, and its depth sets a deadline: how many bad seasons the household can absorb before ruin. A toy shows the consequence. Savings move +1 or −1 each period, and the household can pay 3 now for 6 later. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. At delay 16 and buffer 8, investing raises expected wealth from 8.15 to 10.30 and lowers survival from 0.846 to 0.835. Covering shocks through the delay lowers the threshold to the outlay alone, which is what graduation programmes' consumption support does. The time pressure here is the planning horizon. Deliberation time and attention are a second sense, left to the scarcity readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v4 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) holds an outside supply that repairs the organization and leaves its own capacity alone. The readings say aid does not leave it alone: it does the work the capacity is learned from. Moss, Pettersson and van de Walle cite Kaldor, that a state leaves aid dependency as it "learns how to tax". Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's 1999 model already has taxing experience built by revenue collected and decaying with time, and capacity kept lower the more aid finances. Moore says raising revenue keeps a state's machinery alive at the grassroots. Ostrom et al. find recipients losing skill and rebuilding plants they did not maintain, and Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock find capability stagnating under aid. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. Aid used after capacity, covering only what it cannot yet do, keeps service whole and leaves capacity to grow as if there were no aid. The first point is Azam et al.'s; the second and third are not in their paper. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v6 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) v4 | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. Here learning by doing needs capacity already present, dC/dt = λPC(1 − C) − μC. With λ = 1, μ = 0.3 and τ = 1.5, a party alone keeps C = 0.7, and C below 0.276 decays to nothing. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Tapering such support is worse the slower it is: from C = 0.45 under support doing 95 % of the work, an abrupt cut recovers, a taper over 5 periods recovers, and any taper longer than 9.13 periods traps the party. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. That reconciles Azam et al.'s optimal up-front cut, made for substitutive aid, with the Kenya exit study's success with gradual exits in which participants already did the work. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-714](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-714.md) | A present incapacity to recognize a violation does not show that the incapacitated party is not responsible for the incapacity: where it dismantled the capability in breach of a duty, the incapacity is a consequence of its earlier wrong and does not excuse it, the same failure of responsiveness differs in significance with its history, and where no one is culpable for the incapacity the duty to repair still stands | A's, from A108 §5 ("The surprising tension with Wolf") and A110 §7 ("Why present incapacity cannot settle historical responsibility") of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), building on the owner's U47 point that blame gives provenance for holding upstream actors accountable ([CLAIM-733](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-733.md)). A applies it to one actor across time: CannotDetect_{t₁}(A, r) does not imply NotResponsibleForIncapacity(A, r). The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-715](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-715.md) | Friction that makes the people in a process think before accepting an output differs from friction that makes the institution answerable to their objections, so a system can make individuals think harder while leaving the institution's authority untouched, and the added scrutiny can then serve as evidence that the individuals owned decisions whose conditions they could not change | A's, from A23 §7 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15), developing the owner's U11 ([CLAIM-710](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)): "**A system can make individuals think harder while leaving the institution's authority completely untouched.**" Cognitive friction, as in Buçinca, Malaya and Gajos's cognitive forcing functions ([LIT-2283](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2283.md), read), makes people "think"; political friction makes institutions "answerable" through protected refusal, independent review and suspension. The perverse case: "The system demands that humans exercise judgment, then treats that demand as evidence that the humans owned the resulting decisions", which A calls "a possible *moral crumple zone* mechanism" ([CLAIM-707](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-707.md)). It rests on [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md), on which access to a signal, its authority over action and action on it are separable. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-716](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-716.md) | A breach can lower the injured party's position if it refuses to settle, so that the breaching party gains leverage over the resolution of its own breach: a settlement the injured party rationally accepts afterward can leave the breacher ahead, the leverage coming from the violation and not from any right to set the terms | A's, A55 §3 and §9 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), "**Breach-induced remedial hold-up**", at the owner's U25 ("how does this developing theory model fait accompli contract violation?"), which named the case. [CLAIM-464](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) holds that an act can make a specified corrective outcome costlier or unreachable before review; this adds the bargaining channel, that the same act lowers what the injured party has if it refuses to settle, so the wrongdoer gains leverage over the settlement of its own wrong. A57 §8 names the distinction between remedial externalization and remedial capture, and A61 §5 the resource-mediated form. Interpretive; A55's numbers show the possibility and were checked. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-717](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-717.md) | Blame and repair do not substitute for each other: assigning blame for creating a harmful condition does not discharge the remedial duties of those now responsible for it, and assigning present remedial duties does not show that those who bear them were to blame for it, so that treating one guilty official as a repair of the system is blame displacement, and loading the repair on whoever is nearest is remedial scapegoating | A's, from A110 §8 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), "A responsibility graph, rather than a single attribution of blame", its non-substitution principle, written to develop the owner's U47 distinction between blame and accountability ([CLAIM-742](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-742.md)). The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-719](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-719.md) | An institution can be reliably responsive to reasons within its governing mechanism and unresponsive to justified reasons for revising that mechanism, and because its own actions change the mechanism, responsiveness at the first order is no evidence of responsiveness at the second; identical decisions can come from different capacities to be governed by reasons | A's, from A108 §6 (epistemic, practical and reflexive responsiveness; "*correctable* at the first order but inadequately governable at the second") and A110 §9–10 (a formal model of maintained normative responsiveness, ρ^(1) and ρ^(2)) of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), with A106 §18's identical decisions from different capacities. The definitions are asserted, not derived, and ρ^(2) is named without being defined. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-720](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-720.md) | Inalienability is a limit on normative powers, not on exercise: a person may restrict the exercise of a right or delegate limited authority over decisions, and no delegation, contract, collective decision or success in imposing an arrangement thereby confers authority to determine whether that person keeps the standing from which claims against the arrangement arise, because the holder lacks the power to confer it | A's, A85 §2 and §4 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), at the owner's U37 ([QUESTION-486](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-486.md)): three concepts, "Exercise restriction", "Delegation of authority" and "Alienation of standing", and "**A person may relinquish control over particular decisions without thereby giving another unlimited authority to determine whether that person continues to possess rights.**" A85 marks it "a proposed interpretation of the natural-rights argument", after Locke's Second Treatise §§22–23 and 135 and Hohfeld's immunity. A87 §4 corrects A85's framing: an immunity is a limit on another's power, nonwaivability a limit on the holder's, and inalienability is "a theory of who lacks power over the continued existence of a protected normative relationship". The claim is filed in the corrected form. The record has no entry on inalienability. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-721](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-721.md) | Where competence is kept by use and lost with disuse, and a restriction is to be lifted when competence is shown, a restriction justified by a lack of competence lowers the competence it waits for, so that unless the restricting party supplies a route to practice or training, the restriction produces the evidence for its own continuation | A's, from the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16): A41 §8 ("This is a possible **restriction-induced capability trap**"), restated in A45 §9 and A49 §8.1. | [CLAIM-722](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-722.md) | Succeeding in making a remedy unreachable gains a wrongdoer no normative power over what is owed: a claim still valid under the standard persists while the correctability of its fitting remedy falls to zero, and an acceptance or settlement reached under the conditions the violation created does not by that fact authorize the violation | A's, first stated in A85 §5 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), r_i^N = 1 with α_r ≈ 0, "The moral right remains valid. | [CLAIM-723](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-723.md) | Acting before a recognized opportunity for intervention can take effect is a wrong of its own, apart from acting without consent: where a party has standing to authorize, suspend or contest an act, an actor who without adequate justification makes the act's consequences irreversible before that standing can be exercised defeats it, even where the objection would have failed | The owner's, from U27 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16): "would it help if we formalized the notion of consent violation? maybe something like acting before a recognized opportunity for intervention is able to take effect? | [CLAIM-724](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-724.md) | Against a challenged party who can act on the means of correction, correctability is a robust quantity, the chance that a corrective policy reaches its objective against every strategy in a declared class of opposition, and it depends on who moves first, since a corrector that must commit before seeing the opposition can do strictly worse than one that responds to it; judged against the opposition the procedural rules permit, failure shows the institution inadequate, and failure owed to opposition outside them shows a wrong by the opponent as well | A's, first stated A76 VIII.4 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16) as "Adversarially robust correctability", refined A81 §3 (2026-11-17) with claimant–institution policies and the split Σ_permitted ⊆ Σ_physically available; A90 IX restates it. | [CLAIM-726](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-726.md) | A party can arrange the conditions under which another commits a real wrong and then use the true accusation, before an audience whose judgement it anticipated, to justify further control over them; the truth of the accusation neither vindicates the party that arranged it nor excuses the one who did wrong | A's, from the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15): A7 §5 ("blaming someone for wrongdoing can itself become a means of wrongdoing"), A9 §6's loop, in which a partner punished for disagreeing conceals, the concealment is found and becomes the reason for more surveillance, A11's closing "manufacturing culpability", and A13 §8's "true accusation" made "across two distinct audiences". | [CLAIM-727](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-727.md) | Authority over a decision does not carry authority over the conditions on which it may be challenged: control of the cost, timing, evidence, forum or remedy of a challenge needs its own justification, and where an actor's authority is meant to be constrained by independently justified claims, its own judgment that it has met them cannot always establish that it has | A's, A83 §3E, §7 and close of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), at the owner's U36: "An actor's authority over a substantive decision does not automatically confer authority to determine the conditions under which affected parties may challenge that decision", with the principle of "non-self-certifying authority". | [CLAIM-728](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-728.md) | In an incomplete contract the party holding residual rights of control decides the contingencies the contract did not cover, so a relationship fair in every specified term can still leave one party's terms at the other's discretion, and that discretion is exercised, and seen, only when an uncovered contingency arises | A's, A53 §2 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), at the owner's U24 ("labor theory, contract theory, and auction theory are feeling relevant"): residual control rights, after Grossman and Hart (1986) and Hart and Moore (1990), as "almost a direct economic formulation of our second-order agency thesis", and the question "**When circumstances arise that the existing agreement doesn't cover, who gets to decide what happens next?**" The connection to contract theory is the owner's; the residual-control reading is A's. | [CLAIM-730](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-730.md) | Where a slowly revised governing level (a statute, an objective, a classification) constrains a fast process, the fast process can change the world before the slow level can be revised, so those it harms have no route to the rule as fast as its application reaches them, and the rule dominates them without anyone actively intervening; where the slow level is open to revision on demand, the same separation of timescales keeps the fast process accountable instead | A's, from A33 §4 and §8 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15), after the owner pointed to the record's "timescale separation" (U16): "**A slow variable can govern a fast process, while the fast process changes the world before the slow variable can be revised.**" "This creates the possibility of temporal domination without constant active intervention by a controller." | [CLAIM-731](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-731.md) | The cost of imposing a decision and the cost of questioning, suspending or reversing it are separate, so an institution can lower the first while the second stays the same or rises, gaining power over those its decisions affect with no change in its formal authority: friction moves from the exercise of power to its contestation | A's, from A23 §2 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15), developing the owner's U11 ([CLAIM-710](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)) at the owner's U12 ("flesh this out further"): "**Execution friction:** The difficulty of imposing a decision" and "**Contestation friction:** The difficulty of questioning, suspending, or reversing it." | [CLAIM-732](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-732.md) | A protected objection is effective only if six achievements hold together, its becoming formulable, legible, taken up by an authorized channel, sustainable by the objector, corrected and maintained, so an objection can fail at any of them while its formal standing is unchanged, its chance of success is no greater than that of its weakest stage, and a reform that raises one stage's success can lower the whole | A's, A79 §10 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), "The lifecycle of a protected objection", sharpened A81 §2 and §9 (2026-11-17) and proposed for the record in A81 §14 as "Distributed failure of effective objection". | [CLAIM-733](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-733.md) | Blame supplies provenance: responsibility for a harmful act and responsibility for producing the incapacity through which it was done can come apart and attach to different actors, so blame traced upstream to those who formed or maintained an agent's incapacity grounds holding them accountable where the agent who acted is not culpable | The owner's, from U47 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17): ""blame" gives us provenance for holding upstream actors accountable as well." | [CLAIM-734](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-734.md) | Where an entitlement is protected by a requirement of its holder's consent, an irreversible act against it leaves the holder in practice only a claim to compensation, so the actor has changed by its own act the rule by which the entitlement is allocated, from consent to liability, and not only what is paid for it | From the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16). | [CLAIM-736](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-736.md) | An opposition can be independent as an actor, in its leadership, aims and speech, while its capacity to change the arrangement it opposes depends on another party's control of its resources, standing, corrective authority or time; that controlled incapacity, and not incapacity or failure as such, is what makes a contained opposition a mark of domination | A's, A37 §10 to §11 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), at the owner's U18 ("relate our discussion to controlled opposition"), with A37 §1's three kinds of controlled opposition, §4's three outcomes and §9's evidence as its parts. | [CLAIM-737](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-737.md) | That a capability's exercise should be limited and that a given party may limit it are separate conclusions on separate grounds, neither entailing the other; the power to restrict is itself a capability, whose legitimacy turns on how it is bounded and answerable and not on whether the limit it imposes is right | A's, A45 §6 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16): "The grounds of restriction" and "The authority of restriction", with "The second question is not answered by the first", answering the owner's question at U20 ([QUESTION-478](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-478.md)). | [CLAIM-739](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-739.md) | Answerability is directed and role-specific: an actor owes an answer to a party with a claim concerning the matter, on one of several grounds that need not presuppose the actor's legitimate authority, among them interference with a protected interest, entrusted authority, collective rule, consequential dependence and control over recourse; the party owed, the recipient of reasons, the forum that judges and the party that remedies can differ; and what is owed is indexed to the claim, not to how much the party is affected | A's answer, A83 §§3–5 and §10 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), to the owner's U36 ("when is answerability required of an authority or governing capability? under what conditions is justification owed, to whom, and why?"), [QUESTION-480](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-480.md); A90 IV restates it with the remedier as a fourth role. [CLAIM-687](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md) scales one ground, dependence; [CLAIM-624](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) states the second-order duty that follows when an answer is owed; this says when one is owed and to whom. | [CLAIM-740](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-740.md) | For a party affected by a decision, explanation (understanding why it was reached), contestation (challenging it or the principles behind it) and interruption (suspending its execution while the challenge is considered) are separate entitlements, and each without the next fails in its own way: explanation without contestation is transparency without accountability, contestation without interruption a right that arrives too late, and interruption without reasons an arbitrary veto | A's, from A23 §6 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15), "Explanation, contestation, and interruption are three different rights", developing the owner's U11 ([CLAIM-710](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)) at U12. [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s achievements are an organization's; these are the affected party's entitlements, and [CLAIM-624](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md)'s answerability is what contestation is owed under. | [CLAIM-742](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-742.md) | Blame and accountability are not the same thing: an agent's diminished culpability for the reasons it acts on does not diminish the wrongfulness of what it does, the claims of those it harms, or the need for correction, because the grounds of correction are not exhausted by the grounds of blame | The owner's, from U47 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), answering A108 §5's "JoJo's moral incapacity is meant to complicate our assessment of blame": "perhaps "blame" and "accountability" aren't the same thing. A110 ("Accountability Without Blame") develops it: its four questions and its usage note, its correction of "unintentionally" to "unwitting", and its three assessments are A's and are credited below. "The grounds of correction are not exhausted by the grounds of blame" is A110 §12's compression of the owner's point. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-744](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-744.md) | Where one party gives up something now for a benefit another controls later, whether waiting is good judgment depends on the controller's reliability, so the controller's discretion over delivery is discretion over whether the other's restraint is rational, and a controller not answerable for delivery can make that party's patience a means of its control | A's, A51 §4 and its second candidate proposition in the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), from the owner's association at U23 of self-restraint with the marshmallow test ([CASE-281](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-281.md)): "**The virtue of patience can be exploited by actors who control the conditions under which patience is rewarded.**" A53 §2, at the owner's U24, gives the decision side: wait only if 2pδ > 1, where p is the chance the promise is kept. The record holds the parallel for households, where declining a delayed payoff below a buffer is the right policy and reads as impatience ([CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md)), and the ratchet under limited commitment ([TERM-110](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-110.md)); it had nothing on deferred rewards as a site of control. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-745](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-745.md) | A categorical administrative gate can make evidence that a governing standard requires to count unable to change a decision: an authority that conditions a substantive entitlement on a categorical criterion displaces the reasons its decisions are supposed to answer to, and that the criterion is imposed, and complied with, establishes neither its legal authority nor its justification | A's, from A108 §1 and §4 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), written at the owner's U46, which offered Trump-era immigration policy as a demonstration of an institution manufacturing moral authority through its own requirements. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-746](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-746.md) | Four judgments about an authority are distinct: the warrant of the obligations it is to serve, its jurisdiction over the matter, its arrangement's capacity to realize those obligations together, and its capacity to reach compliant arrangements and correct failures by permitted means; neither of the first two follows from any of the others, and of the last two only the dynamic one implies the static one, for what it reaches | A's, A74 §9 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16), restated A76 X: "I would therefore distinguish four judgments", normative warrant, jurisdictional legitimacy, organizational adequacy and dynamic answerability, which "none should be collapsed into another". It refines A71's triad of legitimacy, adequacy and efficacy, given in answer to the owner's U31 (QUESTION-485), by splitting legitimacy into the warrant of the obligations and the jurisdiction of the actor (CLAIM-737's separation) and adequacy into a static and a dynamic part ([CLAIM-560](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-560.md)'s). The filer corrects A's independence: the dynamic judgment implies the static one for the arrangements it reaches. The wording is A's, as corrected; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-747](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-747.md) | The alternatives against which a governing relationship or principle is assessed can be products of that relationship, so the present distribution of options is not a neutral baseline, and an actor cannot justify its terms by the narrowness of options it helped narrow without justification; the assessment must separate the existence of a dependence, the legitimacy of its creation, the authority exercised through it and the responsibilities of maintaining it | A's, from A102 §6 ("The circumstances of reasonable rejection are themselves shaped by prior exercises of power") and A106 §9 ("The endogeneity problem: Existing circumstances are not a neutral baseline") of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), as pressure on contractualism at the owner's U44. | [CLAIM-748](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-748.md) | Litigation as siege: an actor can make a legally recognized corrective objective unreachable for another party, with the merits, the law and that party's preferences unchanged, by raising what pursuing the objective costs, in spending or in time, above what that party can sustain until relief arrives | The owner's, from U28 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16): "Time is just one resource asymmetry that can be abused here. A61 and A64 formalized it ([CASE-287](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-287.md), rechecked), and A64 opened by telling the owner's point as its own "key insight". | [CLAIM-749](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-749.md) | Influence over others does not by itself ground a duty to answer to them: a legitimate right can assign a decision to its holder, so that an owner may decline to explain choices within a protected sphere however much they affect others, and answerability is owed where the justified structure of a relationship requires it, not wherever an action has effects | A's, from A106 §10 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17), "Private property shows why answerability must be bounded", with A106 §17's last example.
